text:
Karwa Chauth 2025: Significance Of The Kitchen Sieve
Curated By :
Edited By:
Last Updated:
The humble chalni (sieve) is one of the most important aspects of Karwa Chauth. There are several reasons why.
Advertisement
Karwa Chauth will be celebrated on October 10 this year.
1/10
Karwa Chauth is one of the most cherished festivals among married Hindu women, especially in North India. It’s a day marked by fasting, prayer, and rituals performed for the long life and well-being of one’s husband. (Image: Canva)
Advertisement
2/10
Among the many symbolic elements of this tradition, the kitchen sieve (chalni) holds a unique and deeply emotional place, especially during the climactic moon-viewing ceremony. (Image: Canva)
3/10
As the moon rises, women gather—dressed in vibrant traditional attire, adorned with jewellery and mehendi—to perform the final ritual of the day. Holding a decorated thali (plate) with a diya (lamp), water, and sweets, they use the sieve to look at the moon. Immediately after, they turn the sieve toward their husband’s face, viewing him through the same mesh. (Image: AI-Generated)
Advertisement
4/10
This act is not just ceremonial—it’s layered with meaning. The sieve becomes a spiritual filter, a symbolic lens through which the woman sees her world: first the divine (moon), then the earthly (her partner). It marks the transition from devotion to fulfillment, from longing to union. (Image: Pinterest)
5/10
Symbolism and Cultural Meaning
Filtering Out Negativity: Just as a sieve separates impurities from flour, it metaphorically filters out distractions, ego, and negativity—allowing the woman to focus on love, purity, and commitment. (Image: Pinterest)

Advertisement
6/10
Perspective and Clarity: Looking through the sieve represents clarity of vision. It’s a reminder that love and relationships require seeing beyond the surface, through layers of understanding and patience. (Image: Pinterest)
7/10
Connection Between Celestial and Earthly: The moon is often seen as a symbol of calm, beauty, and divine energy. By viewing the moon and then her husband through the same sieve, the woman connects the celestial with the personal, invoking blessings and harmony. (Image: Pinterest)
Advertisement
8/10
A Moment of Emotional Intimacy: This ritual often becomes a tender moment between couples. The husband offers water and sweets to break the fast, symbolizing care and reciprocity. The chalni, in this context, becomes a bridge between sacrifice and love. (Image: Pinterest)
9/10
Popular Culture Influence: Bollywood has played a significant role in romanticizing this ritual. Films like Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham... and Baghban have immortalized the moon-sieve moment, turning it into a visual metaphor for eternal love and devotion. This has further deepened its emotional resonance among younger generations. (Image: Instagram)
